# Module `fs`

fs - filesystem primitives (#195).

Path/fs operations crossing the runtime's `__vyb_*` helpers; the Vyb surface
stays allocation/pointer-free like `io`. Today this is the nested-store
unblocker VybOS needs: a program can create a directory tree so the store can
use a nested layout and write per-derivation metadata next to realised
outputs (replacing the host `freedom { exec } mkdir -p` staging hacks).

Usage:
  import fs::{mkdir}
  match (mkdir("/store/a/b/c")) {
      ok -> { println("created") }
      ?  -> { println("mkdir failed: " + error_message()) }
  }

<a id="sym-mkdir"></a>
### `mkdir` · fn

```
mkdir(path<String>)<Bool?> ->
```

Recursively create `path` (all missing parent components), idempotent when a
component already exists as a directory. Returns `Bool?` -- present on
success, absent on failure (mirrors io's optional `T?` shape; a directory
carries no file descriptor, so presence == success).
